title: Relative Hopf-module data for a coideal quotient
statement: Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field] and $H$ a unital commutative $k$-bialgebra, meaning a commutative $k$-algebra with algebra maps $\Delta:H\to H\otimes_k H$ and $\epsilon:H\to k$ satisfying coassociativity and both counit identities. All module tensors are [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product] and algebra tensors have the structure of [lem-weil-pbc-algebra-tensor-pushout-universal-property]. For a unital $k$-subalgebra $A\subset H$, say it is a right coideal if $\Delta(A)$ is contained in the image of $A\otimes_k H\to H\otimes_k H$. Define $A^+=\ker(\epsilon|_A)$, $J=HA^+$ as the ideal of $H$ spanned by its elements, $Q=H/J$, and $\pi:H\to Q$ as the canonical quotient map. Give $Q$ its quotient ring structure and its multiplication $H$-action. Let $C$ be a $k$-coalgebra and an $H$-module, with compatible underlying $k$-action. For an $H$-module $X$, with its compatible underlying $k$-action, define $T_X:H\otimes_k H\to\operatorname{End}_k(C\otimes_k X)$ by $T_X(g\otimes h)(c\otimes x)=gc\otimes hx$. A relative Hopf-module coaction on $X$ is a $k$-linear map $\alpha:X\to C\otimes_k X$ satisfying $(\Delta_C\otimes1)\alpha=(1\otimes\alpha)\alpha$, $(\epsilon_C\otimes1)\alpha=1_X$, and $\alpha(hx)=T_X(\Delta(h))(\alpha(x))$. For $e\in C$ define its coinvariant set to be $\{x\in X:\alpha(x)=e\otimes x\}$. An $H$-linear map $f:X\to Y$ is a morphism of these coactions if $\alpha_Y f=(1_C\otimes f)\alpha_X$. If $J$ is a coideal, give $Q$ the canonical quotient coalgebra structure. For an $A$-module $M$, with compatible underlying $k$-action, say a relative coaction $\alpha$ on $H\otimes_A M$ is induced if for all $h,m$ it satisfies $\alpha(h\otimes_A m)=(\pi\otimes(t\mapsto t\otimes_A m))(\Delta(h))$. This defines the data and predicates only; the coideal, submodule, induction and kernel assertions are the subsequent theorem, rather than part of this definition.
